## Historical audit: S0075

**Scope.** This audit covers chunk 1 of 2 only. All citations below refer to S0075, original file `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/ours_without_regression_guidance/C1/test/commons_155212263/trajectory.jsonl`. The reference and rendered images themselves are not visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Goal | The student was asked to reconstruct a single indoor photograph using separate meshes, matching camera, framing, materials and contacts. The student interpreted it as a window-side metalworking workshop; that interpretation is not independent image verification. (Student request, JSONL line 1; student response, line 3.) |
| Initial build | The program specified multiple benches, two flywheel assemblies, an anvil, a lathe, vices, drawer, containers, architecture and clutter. It used grouped parts, explicit coordinates and intended worktop contact heights, rather than persistent binds. It specified wood/iron colors, procedural bump, luminous glass, an oblique camera and two area lights. These are code-level intentions, not proof of visible objects, correct part connections or pose. (Student response line 3; execute step 1, line 4.) |
| Interruption and repair | Step 1 timed out after approximately 600 seconds, with empty stdout/stderr and no image. The runner told the student not to diagnose an unseen image and to repair the program. The student replaced individually modeled floorboards with a shader, reduced repeated details and samples, and executed step 2. Complexity was the student’s repair hypothesis; the timeout did not establish its cause. (Execution result line 5; student request line 6; response line 8; execute line 9.) |
| Validation | Step 2 returned `ok: true`, reported a saved PNG and blend file, and a select event recorded step 2. The log reports 16 samples despite the program specifying 24. Successful execution is not verification of framing, materials, geometry or contacts. (Execution result line 10, characters [0,110053); select line 11.) |
| Autonomous revision | After the reference and step-2 render were supplied, the student described too much room, small machinery and an exposed wall top, and hypothesized a closer, lower-aimed camera would improve framing and parallax. The executed step 3 retained the lens but changed camera position and aim; it also changed floor-shader coordinates and mortar width, so it was not solely a camera change. Those visual diagnoses are student claims, not independently checked here. (Student request line 12, characters [0,152801); student response line 14; execute line 15.) |

**Teacher input and adoption.** No separate teacher message is visible in this chunk. The runner’s timeout-repair and render-review instructions were received in student requests; the subsequent simplification and camera revision show corresponding action, not receipt of any separate teacher guidance. Student sessions report zero tool calls; the visible exploration is program generation, execution and image-review-driven revision, not external research (lines 2, 6–9, 12–15).

**Outcome and uncertainty.** The visible record establishes a technical interruption followed by a formally successful step 2 and selection of that step. Step 3 was executed, but its result and the final outcome are outside this chunk. Visual correctness—including multiple-object visibility, textures, actual connections, object poses, camera match and lighting—is unknown. A transferable lesson is that a timeout can motivate a simpler representation and retry without treating a missing render as visual evidence; here, the specific bottleneck remains unresolved. The workshop inventory and claimed framing defects remain task-specific hypotheses.
